summary: 英国圣诞童话剧融合歌舞、笑料与童话，从意大利即兴喜剧吸收了弱者获胜的故事传统。英国表演者又陆续加入舞台奇观、白脸小丑和男扮女装的主角，使这种家庭娱乐得以延续。
logic: 英国剧场的表演与争议

sentences: A pantomime performance is a unique blend of eccentricity and absurdity, a wild mixture of songs, jokes, outrageous costumes and slapstick physical humour.
超凡表演是怪异和荒谬的独特结合，狂野的歌曲、笑话、令人憎恶的服装和拍掌的幽默。
For many British children, their first family trip to see a pantomime in the Christmas holiday season is their introduction to the magic of the theatre.
对于许多英国儿童来说，他们在圣诞节假期第一次参加全息旅行，就是介绍戏剧的魔力。
But what has become a quintessentially British form of entertainment is more than just simple fun.
但英国的娱乐形式不仅仅是简单的乐趣
As an art form, pantomime presents a tale of good and evil, where hope finally triumphs after danger and virtual despair.
作为一种艺术形式，Pantomime 展示了一个善恶的故事，在那里，希望最终在危险和实际上的绝望之后获胜。

paragraphs.brief: 户外演出与固定的一组角色。
sentences: The story of pantomime begins with the commedia dell’arte tradition in 16th-century Italy.
以16世纪意大利的共和媒体Dell’arte传统为起点。
These improvised shows took place in streets and marketplaces in Italy and eventually throughout Europe.
这些即兴表演在意大利的街道和市场中进行，最终在欧洲各地进行。
Distinctive masks enabled audiences to recognise the people in these stories immediately; they also allowed actors to be rude or disrespectful without fear of being recognised.
不同的面具使听众能够立即认出这些故事中的人；他们还允许演员无礼或不尊重，而不必担心被认出。
The key roles in the cast were invariably rich old men, usually portrayed as cowardly and disreputable; young lovers whose parents refuse to let them marry; and ingenious and quick-witted servants.
演员中的主要角色总是富豪老人，通常被描绘成懦弱和无声无息的；年轻情人，其父母拒绝让他们结婚；巧妙和聪明的仆人。
Many commedia plots show the latter, whose lives are a constant struggle to find food and money, outwitting the old men or overthrowing their masters.
许多媒体的图谋都向后者展示，他们的生活是不断为寻找食物和金钱而奋斗，是愚弄老人或推翻主人。
This theme of the victory of the underdog is still an essential feature of pantomime today.
胜利的这个主题弱者仍然是今天的全局性的基本特征。

paragraphs.brief: 不同艺术元素的成功融合。
sentences: By the mid-18th century, many thousands of people were going to theatres across Britain every night.
到18世纪中叶成千上万的人每天晚上都会去英国的剧院
Among the most popular performances were harlequinades, a new kind of entertainment which interwove Ovid’s first-century Latin poem Metamorphoses with aspects of the Italian commedia.
在最受欢迎的表演中，有哈勒奎娜(harlequinades)，这是一种新型娱乐活动，将奥维德第一世纪的拉丁诗《Metamophose》与意大利的媒体内容交织在一起。
Created by actor John Rich, these early pantomimes cleverly mixed spectacle, music, ballet and myth, and were tremendously enjoyable to watch.
由演员约翰·里奇创造这些早期的短片精巧地混合了景象音乐芭蕾和神话
Amazing transformations happened at the touch of a magic wand, with mechanical serpents and flying vehicles.
神奇的转变发生在魔杖的触碰下机械蛇和飞行器
They also showed that even early pantomime was fascinated by the crossing of boundaries: the ambiguity of men dressed as women, and the fun of animal characters played by human beings.
他们还显示，即使早期的无所事事也因跨越边界而着迷：穿成女性的男子模棱两可，以及人类玩弄动物角色的乐趣。

paragraphs.brief: 如何应对人们对童话剧的偏见。
sentences: Despite their popularity, Rich’s spectacular performances attracted huge controversy.
富人的壮观表演吸引了巨大的争议。
Critics bitterly attacked pantomimes, complaining that they would bring about the downfall of Shakespeare and the death of serious theatre.
批评者们严厉攻击了全神贯注者，抱怨说，他们将带来莎士比亚的垮台和严重戏剧的死。
David Garrick, the great 18th-century actor-manager, was quick to join these criticisms, while also realising the commercial opportunities of this new art form.
18世纪伟大的演员管理者大卫·加里克很快地加入了这些批评同时也实现了这种新艺术形式的商业机会
But how could Garrick take advantage of the craze and still maintain his position as the defender of ‘legitimate’ theatre?
但Garrick怎么能利用狂欢并保持他作为"合法"剧院的捍卫者的地位呢？
His tactic was to set about changing pantomime’s cultural identity, partly by confining shows to his theatre’s Christmas season.
他的策略是改变全美文化特性部分方式是限制剧场的圣诞季演出
Pantomimes became associated with the frivolity of the holiday season rather than being denounced as a threat.
泛神论与节日的杂乱无章有关，而不是被谴责为威胁。
In doing so, Garrick created a convention which has survived to this day.
加里克在这样做时创立了一项公约，至今仍得以维持。

paragraphs.brief: 借童话剧聚焦政治议题。
sentences: At the end of the 18th century, popular theatre saw the arrival of the white-faced Clown, in the form of actor Joseph Grimaldi.
18世纪末流行剧院看到了白脸小丑的到来演员约瑟夫·格里马尔迪
By the early 19th century, Britain was at war with France; there was intense civil unrest and violent confrontations between the government and the people.
到19世纪初，英国与法国交战；政府和人民之间发生了激烈的内乱和暴力对抗。
Grimaldi’s hilarious antics embodied the freedom and liberty of British culture by contrast with the country’s supposedly dull, humourless enemies.
与英国所谓无趣、无趣的敌人形成对比的是，格里马尔迪的可笑的狂欢情绪体现了英国文化的自由和自由。
His anarchic activities included chasing and imprisoning policemen and stealing gigantic quantities of sausages.
他的无政府活动包括追逐和监禁警察以及偷窃大量的香肠。
But the Clown was never caught or sent to jail.
但小丑从未被抓或被送进监狱

Audiences were thrilled by his mischief and his endless eating precisely because he created on stage the fantasy of a different world: a world without hunger, a world of comic revenge against a highly repressive government.
观众对他的恶作剧和无休止的饮食感到兴奋，正是因为他在舞台上创造了一个不同世界的幻想：一个没有饥饿的世界，一个对高度镇压性政府进行连环报复的漫画世界。
Grimaldi became one of the great satirists of his age, a character who offered ludicrous commentaries on everything from the ruling classes to fashion, technology and new forms of transport.
格里马尔迪成为他这个时代的伟大讽刺家之一，此人对从统治阶级到时装、技术和新运输方式的一切都给出了荒谬的评论。

paragraphs.brief: 同时让人同情又发笑的角色。
sentences: By the late 19th century, photography had arrived, the telegraph had been invented and the first motor cars were starting to appear on British streets.
到了19世纪末摄影已经到来电报已经发明第一批汽车开始出现在英国街头

Meanwhile, the spotlight on the comic stage shifted away from the Clown and towards an unexpected star, the pantomime ‘Dame’: a tired housewife – always played by a man – struggling to cope in an unfriendly world.
同时，漫画舞台上的焦点从小丑转向一个出乎意料的明星，即“Dame”:一个疲惫的家庭主妇 — — 总是由男人扮演 — — 在一个不友好的世界中挣扎。

Dan Leno was the celebrated performer who created and played this talkative and eccentric working-class woman, a mother facing the difficulties of poverty, which he and his audiences knew all too well.
Dan Leno是著名的表演家创造并扮演了这个说话又古怪的工人阶级女人，母亲面对贫困的困难，他和他的观众都非常清楚。
In the Dame, Leno developed a persona whose theatrical power comes from the locking together of compassion and laughter.
在圣母院里，莱诺发展了一个人，其戏剧力量来自团结在一起的同情和笑声。
At the same time, artists such as Leno began to infuse pantomime with the plots and dilemmas of working people’s culture.
诸如Leno等艺术家也开始用劳动人民文化的阴谋和两难处境来装扮成一团糟。

paragraphs.brief: 一个童话剧角色为何能吸引现代观众。
sentences: Pantomimes are as popular today as they have ever been.
今天的万神节和以前一样流行
Our delight in this form comes from a complex mixture of emotions and relationships.
我们这种形式的喜悦来自于情感和关系之间的复杂结合。
Pantomime offers us the anarchic excitements of a topsy-turvy world only to give us the assurance of harmony restored.
Pantomime给我们提供了无政府状态的兴奋在一个混乱的世界中只是为了给我们恢复和谐的保证
The engaging character of the Dame exemplifies pantomime’s self-proclaimed absurdity.
女神的热衷性证明了她自封的荒谬
Her comical conversations with the audience cut across the boundaries between performers and spectators, drawing us into her chaotic world.
她和观众的滑稽谈话跨越了表演者与观众之间的界限把我们引入她混乱的世界
While she presides over the anarchy which Grimaldi once visited on policemen, the Dame also embodies the collective ties which bind us together as families, as neighbours, and as members of society.
当她主持格里马尔迪曾经访问过警察的无政府状态时，圣母还体现了将我们作为家庭、邻居和社会成员联系在一起的集体纽带。

flow: 从英国孩子的初体验追溯意大利源头
作者从英国儿童熟悉的圣诞演出写起，再往前追到意大利街头戴面具、反复登场的固定角色。
看英国舞台怎样接住这门表演
里奇融入变景和舞台奇观吸引观众，加里克则把演出定位为节庆节目，回应外界批评。
从两位演员看角色如何变化
格里马尔迪用小丑讽刺权威，丹·莱诺的丑角夫人则让观众在笑声中对人物产生同情。
解释旧角色为何留得下来
丑角夫人能直接与台下观众说笑，这种亲密的互动说明今天的家庭观众为何仍愿意看她登台。

items.en: Commedia dell’arte actors used ________ to disguise their real identities.
items.zh: 意大利即兴喜剧的演员用________掩饰自己的真实身份。
items.why: 题干“disguise real identities (伪装身份)” 对应“without fear of being recognised (不怕被认出)”。原文唯一直接工具词是 masks。

items.en: Harlequinades combined elements of a 16th-century art form with a ________ written many centuries earlier.
items.zh: 以丑角阿尔莱金为主角的滑稽戏，把十六世纪一种艺术形式中的元素与早在数百年前写成的一篇________结合起来。
items.why: 回到对应内容“在最受欢迎的表演中，有哈勒奎娜(harlequinades)，这是一种新型娱乐活动，将奥维德第一世纪的拉丁诗《Metamophose》与意大利的媒体内容交织在一起”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In early 19th-century pantomimes, ________ were often victims of the Clown’s activities.
items.zh: 十九世纪初的哑剧中，________常是小丑捉弄的对象。
items.why: “victims (受害者) ”在原文以被追赶、被关押体现，直接指向 policemen。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: His performances focused on the situation of the less wealthy sections of society.
items.zh: 他的工作重点是社会较不富裕阶层的状况。

items.en: He introduced elements of the supernatural to the pantomime genre.
items.zh: 他把超自然元素引入了超自然的流派中

items.en: His pantomime character was never seen to be punished for his on-stage crimes.
items.zh: 他的无耻性格从未被看成是因为他在舞台上的罪行而受到惩罚

pairs: 面具隐藏演员的真实身份，因此他们无需担心被人认出。两处从动作和结果讲同一件事。
interwove 本义是“交织”，在剧目创作中指把诗歌与意大利即兴喜剧融合在一起。
never caught or sent to jail
原文写小丑从未被抓或入狱，题干把这些具体后果概括成“没有受到惩罚”。
points: 意大利即兴喜剧在街头和市集上演，观众凭面具就能辨认反复登场的角色。
题干“disguise real identities (伪装身份)” 对应“without fear of being recognised (不怕被认出)”。原文唯一直接工具词是 masks。
clauses: As an art form, pantomime presents a tale of good and evil, ….
“where hope finally triumphs after danger and virtual despair”修饰前面的 pantomime。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 where 时，回看 pantomime，再把修饰信息接回主句。
“that they would bring about the downfall of Shakespeare and the death of serious theatre”补足 complaining 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 complaining 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
